# Guam Coconut Chicken Adobo 🇬🇺

::: {.dish-meta}
**Region:** Guam & the Marianas (with Filipino roots)  ·  **Family:** Vinegar braise, served over rice
**Serves:** 4  ·  **Active time:** 25 minutes  ·  **Total:** 45 minutes
**Assembly:** 🍚 Chicken over rice — adobo braised, then spooned over steamed rice
:::

Adobo is the great vinegar-and-garlic braise of the Philippines, and it's just as
beloved across Guam and the Marianas, where it's a fixture of the CHamoru table.
This island version enriches the tangy braise with **coconut milk** — abundant in
the Pacific — for a mellow, glossy sauce that begs to be spooned over hot rice.

## The story

At its heart, adobo is a technique as much as a dish: meat simmered in vinegar,
garlic, and bay until tender, then reduced to a punchy, savory glaze. It came to
the Marianas along the deep, centuries-old currents of migration between the
Philippines and Guam, and became a staple of CHamoru home cooking (*adobu*) in its
own right.

What makes this one an *island* adobo is the coconut. Stirred in at the end, thick
coconut milk softens adobo's bracing sourness into something rounder and richer,
without losing that signature tang. Sear the braised chicken until the skin
crackles, fold it back into the sauce, and serve it — as it always is — over a
mound of steaming white rice.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Adapted** from the coconut chicken adobo recipe at
[Cinnamon Society](https://cinnamonsociety.com/recipes/filipino-coconut-chicken-adobo),
tuned to the book's format and made gluten-free and dairy-free.
:::

## Ingredients

- 2½ lb (1.1 kg) bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 8 pieces)
- ½ cup (120 ml) white vinegar
- 2 cups (475 ml) water
- 2 tbsp fish sauce (or **gluten-free tamari or coconut aminos**)
- 3 cloves garlic, smashed
- 1 bay leaf
- ¾ cup (180 ml) thick coconut milk
- ½ tsp paprika
- ½ tsp ground cayenne (adjust to taste)
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp peanut or vegetable oil

**To serve:** steamed white rice, and sliced scallions if you like

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Gluten-free · dairy-free:** naturally dairy-free — the richness is coconut milk.
For gluten-free, reach for **fish sauce, coconut aminos, or gluten-free tamari**
instead of regular soy sauce, and check the label as always.
:::

## Method

1. **Braise.** In a Dutch oven or deep pan, combine the chicken, vinegar, water,
   fish sauce (or tamari), garlic, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower to a
   simmer and cook **uncovered 25–30 minutes**, until the chicken is tender. Let the
   sharp smell of the vinegar cook off as it goes.
2. **Reduce.** Lift the chicken onto a plate and blot it dry. Turn the heat to high
   and boil the braising liquid down for about **10 minutes**, until it's thick
   enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the coconut milk, paprika, cayenne, and black
   pepper; simmer to a glossy sauce.
3. **Sear.** Heat the oil in a wok or skillet over high heat. Sear the chicken
   skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp, about **2 minutes per side**.
4. **Finish.** Return the seared chicken to the sauce and turn to coat. Serve hot,
   spooned over steamed rice with the sauce poured generously on top.

## Make it yours

- **Classic (no coconut):** skip the coconut milk for a sharper, traditional
  Filipino-style adobo — reduce the braise a little less so there's sauce for the
  rice.
- **CHamoru table:** serve alongside *finadene* (a soy-vinegar-chili-onion dipping
  sauce) and red rice for a Guam-style plate.
- **Deeper color:** a splash more tamari or a teaspoon of coconut sugar in the
  reduction gives a darker, slightly sweeter glaze.
- Adobo only improves overnight — make it a day ahead and rewarm gently.
